paragraphs.text: Now it came to pass in those days, there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be enrolled.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐξῆλθεν δόγμα παρὰ Καίσαρος Αὐγούστου ἀπογράφεσθαι πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην·
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de en tais hēmerais ekeinais exēlthen dogma para Kaisaros Augoustou apographesthai pasan tēn oikoumenēn·

paragraphs.text: This was the first enrolment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
paragraphs.original: (αὕτη ἀπογραφὴ πρώτη ἐγένετο ἡγεμονεύοντος τῆς Συρίας Κυρηνίου·)
paragraphs.translit: (hautē apographē prōtē egeneto hēgemoneuontos tēs Syrias Kyrēniou·)

paragraphs.text: And all went to enrol themselves, every one to his own city.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπορεύοντο πάντες ἀπογράφεσθαι, ἕκαστος εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ πόλιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eporeuonto pantes apographesthai, hekastos eis tēn heautou polin.

paragraphs.text: And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David;
paragraphs.original: Ἀνέβη δὲ καὶ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐκ πόλεως Ναζαρὲθ εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν εἰς πόλιν Δαυὶδ ἥτις καλεῖται Βηθλέεμ, διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐξ οἴκου καὶ πατριᾶς Δαυίδ,
paragraphs.translit: Anebē de kai Iōsēph apo tēs Galilaias ek poleōs Nazareth eis tēn Ioudaian eis polin Dauid hētis kaleitai Bēthleem, dia to einai auton ex oikou kai patrias Dauid,

paragraphs.text: to enrol himself with Mary, who was betrothed to him, being great with child.
paragraphs.original: ἀπογράψασθαι σὺν Μαριὰμ τῇ ἐμνηστευμένῃ αὐτῷ, οὔσῃ ἐγκύῳ.
paragraphs.translit: apograpsasthai syn Mariam tē emnēsteumenē autō, ousē enkyō.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, while they were there, the days were fulfilled that she should be delivered.
paragraphs.original: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἐκεῖ ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ τεκεῖν αὐτήν,
paragraphs.translit: egeneto de en tō einai autous ekei eplēsthēsan hai hēmerai tou tekein autēn,

paragraphs.text: And she brought forth her firstborn son; and she wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔτεκεν τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς τὸν πρωτότοκον, καὶ ἐσπαργάνωσεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀνέκλινεν αὐτὸν ἐν φάτνῃ, διότι οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τόπος ἐν τῷ καταλύματι.
paragraphs.translit: kai eteken ton hyion autēs ton prōtotokon, kai esparganōsen auton kai aneklinen auton en phatnē, dioti ouk ēn autois topos en tō katalymati.

paragraphs.text: And there were shepherds in the same country abiding in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ποιμένες ἦσαν ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ τῇ αὐτῇ ἀγραυλοῦντες καὶ φυλάσσοντες φυλακὰς τῆς νυκτὸς ἐπὶ τὴν ποίμνην αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai poimenes ēsan en tē chōra tē autē agraulountes kai phylassontes phylakas tēs nyktos epi tēn poimnēn autōn.

paragraphs.text: And an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐπέστη αὐτοῖς καὶ δόξα κυρίου περιέλαμψεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν·
paragraphs.translit: kai angelos kyriou epestē autois kai doxa kyriou perielampsen autous, kai ephobēthēsan phobon megan·

paragraphs.text: And the angel said unto them, Be not afraid; for behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy which shall be to all the people:
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ ἄγγελος· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε, ἰδοὺ γὰρ εὐαγγελίζομαι ὑμῖν χαρὰν μεγάλην ἥτις ἔσται παντὶ τῷ λαῷ,
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois ho angelos· Mē phobeisthe, idou gar euangelizomai hymin charan megalēn hētis estai panti tō laō,

paragraphs.text: for there is born to you this day in the city of David a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐτέχθη ὑμῖν σήμερον σωτὴρ ὅς ἐστιν χριστὸς κύριος ἐν πόλει Δαυίδ·
paragraphs.translit: hoti etechthē hymin sēmeron sōtēr hos estin christos kyrios en polei Dauid·

paragraphs.text: And this [is] the sign unto you: Ye shall find a babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, and lying in a manger.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τοῦτο ὑμῖν τὸ σημεῖον, εὑρήσετε βρέφος ἐσπαργανωμένον καὶ κείμενον ἐν φάτνῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai touto hymin to sēmeion, heurēsete brephos esparganōmenon kai keimenon en phatnē.

paragraphs.text: And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξαίφνης ἐγένετο σὺν τῷ ἀγγέλῳ πλῆθος στρατιᾶς οὐρανίου αἰνούντων τὸν θεὸν καὶ λεγόντων·
paragraphs.translit: kai exaiphnēs egeneto syn tō angelō plēthos stratias ouraniou ainountōn ton theon kai legontōn·

paragraphs.text: Glory to God in the highest, And on earth peace among men in whom he is well pleased.
paragraphs.original: Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκίας.
paragraphs.translit: Doxa en hypsistois theō kai epi gēs eirēnē en anthrōpois eudokias.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, when the angels went away from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another, Let us now go even unto Bethlehem, and see this thing that is come to pass, which the Lord hath made known unto us.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἀπῆλθον ἀπʼ αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οἱ ἄγγελοι, οἱ ποιμένες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Διέλθωμεν δὴ ἕως Βηθλέεμ καὶ ἴδωμεν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο τὸ γεγονὸς ὃ ὁ κύριος ἐγνώρισεν ἡμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto hōs apēlthon apʼ autōn eis ton ouranon hoi angeloi, hoi poimenes elaloun pros allēlous· Dielthōmen dē heōs Bēthleem kai idōmen to rhēma touto to gegonos ho ho kyrios egnōrisen hēmin.

paragraphs.text: And they came with haste, and found both Mary and Joseph, and the babe lying in the manger.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦλθαν σπεύσαντες καὶ ἀνεῦραν τήν τε Μαριὰμ καὶ τὸν Ἰωσὴφ καὶ τὸ βρέφος κείμενον ἐν τῇ φάτνῃ·
paragraphs.translit: kai ēlthan speusantes kai aneuran tēn te Mariam kai ton Iōsēph kai to brephos keimenon en tē phatnē·

paragraphs.text: And when they saw it, they made known concerning the saying which was spoken to them about this child.
paragraphs.original: ἰδόντες δὲ ἐγνώρισαν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ λαληθέντος αὐτοῖς περὶ τοῦ παιδίου τούτου.
paragraphs.translit: idontes de egnōrisan peri tou rhēmatos tou lalēthentos autois peri tou paidiou toutou.

paragraphs.text: And all that heard it wondered at the things which were spoken unto them by the shepherds.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν περὶ τῶν λαληθέντων ὑπὸ τῶν ποιμένων πρὸς αὐτούς,
paragraphs.translit: kai pantes hoi akousantes ethaumasan peri tōn lalēthentōn hypo tōn poimenōn pros autous,

paragraphs.text: But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ Μαρία πάντα συνετήρει τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα συμβάλλουσα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: hē de Maria panta synetērei ta rhēmata tauta symballousa en tē kardia autēs.

paragraphs.text: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, even as it was spoken unto them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑπέστρεψαν οἱ ποιμένες δοξάζοντες καὶ αἰνοῦντες τὸν θεὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἤκουσαν καὶ εἶδον καθὼς ἐλαλήθη πρὸς αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai hypestrepsan hoi poimenes doxazontes kai ainountes ton theon epi pasin hois ēkousan kai eidon kathōs elalēthē pros autous.

paragraphs.text: And when eight days were fulfilled for circumcising him, his name was called JESUS, which was so called by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ τοῦ περιτεμεῖν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦς, τὸ κληθὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγγέλου πρὸ τοῦ συλλημφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote eplēsthēsan hēmerai oktō tou peritemein auton, kai eklēthē to onoma autou Iēsous, to klēthen hypo tou angelou pro tou syllēmphthēnai auton en tē koilia.

paragraphs.text: And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως, ἀνήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παραστῆσαι τῷ κυρίῳ,
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote eplēsthēsan hai hēmerai tou katharismou autōn kata ton nomon Mōyseōs, anēgagon auton eis Hierosolyma parastēsai tō kyriō,

paragraphs.text: (as it is written in the law of the Lord, Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord),
paragraphs.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν νόμῳ κυρίου ὅτι Πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον μήτραν ἅγιον τῷ κυρίῳ κληθήσεται,
paragraphs.translit: kathōs gegraptai en nomō kyriou hoti Pan arsen dianoigon mētran hagion tō kyriō klēthēsetai,

paragraphs.text: and to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τοῦ δοῦναι θυσίαν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ κυρίου, ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νοσσοὺς περιστερῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai tou dounai thysian kata to eirēmenon en tō nomō kyriou, zeugos trygonōn ē dyo nossous peristerōn.

paragraphs.text: And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon; and this man was righteous and devout, looking for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος ἦν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ ᾧ ὄνομα Συμεών, καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος καὶ εὐλαβής, προσδεχόμενος παράκλησιν τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, καὶ πνεῦμα ἦν ἅγιον ἐπʼ αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: Kai idou anthrōpos ēn en Ierousalēm hō onoma Symeōn, kai ho anthrōpos houtos dikaios kai eulabēs, prosdechomenos paraklēsin tou Israēl, kai pneuma ēn hagion epʼ auton·

paragraphs.text: And it had been revealed unto him by the Holy Spirit, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord`s Christ.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχρηματισμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον πρὶν ἢ ἂν ἴδῃ τὸν χριστὸν κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēn autō kechrēmatismenon hypo tou pneumatos tou hagiou mē idein thanaton prin ē an idē ton christon kyriou.

paragraphs.text: And he came in the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, that they might do concerning him after the custom of the law,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦλθεν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ ἐν τῷ εἰσαγαγεῖν τοὺς γονεῖς τὸ παιδίον Ἰησοῦν τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτοὺς κατὰ τὸ εἰθισμένον τοῦ νόμου περὶ αὐτοῦ
paragraphs.translit: kai ēlthen en tō pneumati eis to hieron· kai en tō eisagagein tous goneis to paidion Iēsoun tou poiēsai autous kata to eithismenon tou nomou peri autou

paragraphs.text: then he received him into his arms, and blessed God, and said,
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδέξατο αὐτὸ εἰς τὰς ἀγκάλας καὶ εὐλόγησεν τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶπεν·
paragraphs.translit: kai autos edexato auto eis tas ankalas kai eulogēsen ton theon kai eipen·

paragraphs.text: Now lettest thou thy servant depart, Lord, According to thy word, in peace;
paragraphs.original: Νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δοῦλόν σου, δέσποτα, κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ·
paragraphs.translit: Nyn apolyeis ton doulon sou, despota, kata to rhēma sou en eirēnē·

paragraphs.text: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation,
paragraphs.original: ὅτι εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου
paragraphs.translit: hoti eidon hoi ophthalmoi mou to sōtērion sou

paragraphs.text: Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples;
paragraphs.original: ὃ ἡτοίμασας κατὰ πρόσωπον πάντων τῶν λαῶν,
paragraphs.translit: ho hētoimasas kata prosōpon pantōn tōn laōn,

paragraphs.text: A light for revelation to the Gentiles, And the glory of thy people Israel.
paragraphs.original: φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν ἐθνῶν καὶ δόξαν λαοῦ σου Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: phōs eis apokalypsin ethnōn kai doxan laou sou Israēl.

paragraphs.text: And his father and his mother were marvelling at the things which were spoken concerning him;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ θαυμάζοντες ἐπὶ τοῖς λαλουμένοις περὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēn ho patēr autou kai hē mētēr thaumazontes epi tois laloumenois peri autou.

paragraphs.text: and Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, Behold, this [child] is set for the falling and the rising of many in Israel; and for a sign which is spoken against;
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς Συμεὼν καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς Μαριὰμ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ· Ἰδοὺ οὗτος κεῖται εἰς πτῶσιν καὶ ἀνάστασιν πολλῶν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ εἰς σημεῖον ἀντιλεγόμενον,
paragraphs.translit: kai eulogēsen autous Symeōn kai eipen pros Mariam tēn mētera autou· Idou houtos keitai eis ptōsin kai anastasin pollōn en tō Israēl kai eis sēmeion antilegomenon,

paragraphs.text: yea and a sword shall pierce through thine own soul; that thoughts out of many hearts may be revealed.
paragraphs.original: καὶ σοῦ δὲ αὐτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν διελεύσεται ῥομφαία, ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶσιν ἐκ πολλῶν καρδιῶν διαλογισμοί.
paragraphs.translit: kai sou de autēs tēn psychēn dieleusetai rhomphaia, hopōs an apokalyphthōsin ek pollōn kardiōn dialogismoi.

paragraphs.text: And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was of a great age, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἦν Ἅννα προφῆτις, θυγάτηρ Φανουήλ, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσήρ (αὕτη προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ἡμέραις πολλαῖς, ζήσασα μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἔτη ἑπτὰ ἀπὸ τῆς παρθενίας αὐτῆς,
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēn Hanna prophētis, thygatēr Phanouēl, ek phylēs Asēr (hautē probebēkyia en hēmerais pollais, zēsasa meta andros etē hepta apo tēs parthenias autēs,

paragraphs.text: and she had been a widow even unto fourscore and four years), who departed not from the temple, worshipping with fastings and supplications night and day.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὴ χήρα ἕως ἐτῶν ὀγδοήκοντα τεσσάρων,) ἣ οὐκ ἀφίστατο τοῦ ἱεροῦ νηστείαις καὶ δεήσεσιν λατρεύουσα νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν.
paragraphs.translit: kai autē chēra heōs etōn ogdoēkonta tessarōn,) hē ouk aphistato tou hierou nēsteiais kai deēsesin latreuousa nykta kai hēmeran.

paragraphs.text: And coming up at that very hour she gave thanks unto God, and spake of him to all them that were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐπιστᾶσα ἀνθωμολογεῖτο τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ πᾶσιν τοῖς προσδεχομένοις λύτρωσιν Ἰερουσαλήμ.
paragraphs.translit: kai autē tē hōra epistasa anthōmologeito tō theō kai elalei peri autou pasin tois prosdechomenois lytrōsin Ierousalēm.

paragraphs.text: And when they had accomplished all things that were according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὡς ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ κατὰ τὸν νόμον κυρίου, ἐπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς πόλιν ἑαυτῶν Ναζαρέθ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hōs etelesan panta ta kata ton nomon kyriou, epestrepsan eis tēn Galilaian eis polin heautōn Nazareth.

paragraphs.text: And the child grew, and waxed strong, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.
paragraphs.original: Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πληρούμενον σοφίᾳ, καὶ χάρις θεοῦ ἦν ἐπʼ αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: To de paidion ēuxanen kai ekrataiouto plēroumenon sophia, kai charis theou ēn epʼ auto.

paragraphs.text: And his parents went every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the passover.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐπορεύοντο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ κατʼ ἔτος εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ τῇ ἑορτῇ τοῦ πάσχα.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eporeuonto hoi goneis autou katʼ etos eis Ierousalēm tē heortē tou pascha.

paragraphs.text: And when he was twelve years old, they went up after the custom of the feast;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἀναβαινόντων αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἑορτῆς
paragraphs.translit: kai hote egeneto etōn dōdeka, anabainontōn autōn kata to ethos tēs heortēs

paragraphs.text: and when they had fulfilled the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem; and his parents knew it not;
paragraphs.original: καὶ τελειωσάντων τὰς ἡμέρας, ἐν τῷ ὑποστρέφειν αὐτοὺς ὑπέμεινεν Ἰησοῦς ὁ παῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai teleiōsantōn tas hēmeras, en tō hypostrephein autous hypemeinen Iēsous ho pais en Ierousalēm, kai ouk egnōsan hoi goneis autou.

paragraphs.text: but supposing him to be in the company, they went a day`s journey; and they sought for him among their kinsfolk and acquaintance:
paragraphs.original: νομίσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν τῇ συνοδίᾳ ἦλθον ἡμέρας ὁδὸν καὶ ἀνεζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γνωστοῖς,
paragraphs.translit: nomisantes de auton einai en tē synodia ēlthon hēmeras hodon kai anezētoun auton en tois syngeneusin kai tois gnōstois,

paragraphs.text: and when they found him not, they returned to Jerusalem, seeking for him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀναζητοῦντες αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē heurontes hypestrepsan eis Ierousalēm anazētountes auton.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both hearing them, and asking them questions:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς εὗρον αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καθεζόμενον ἐν μέσῳ τῶν διδασκάλων καὶ ἀκούοντα αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπερωτῶντα αὐτούς·
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto meta hēmeras treis heuron auton en tō hierō kathezomenon en mesō tōn didaskalōn kai akouonta autōn kai eperōtōnta autous·

paragraphs.text: and all that heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
paragraphs.original: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῇ συνέσει καὶ ταῖς ἀποκρίσεσιν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: existanto de pantes hoi akouontes autou epi tē synesei kai tais apokrisesin autou.

paragraphs.text: And when they saw him, they were astonished; and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I sought thee sorrowing.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεπλάγησαν, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ· Τέκνον, τί ἐποίησας ἡμῖν οὕτως; ἰδοὺ ὁ πατήρ σου καὶ ἐγὼ ὀδυνώμενοι ἐζητοῦμέν σε.
paragraphs.translit: kai idontes auton exeplagēsan, kai eipen pros auton hē mētēr autou· Teknon, ti epoiēsas hēmin houtōs; idou ho patēr sou kai egō odynōmenoi ezētoumen se.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? knew ye not that I must be in my Father`s house?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί ὅτι ἐζητεῖτέ με; οὐκ ᾔδειτε ὅτι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ πατρός μου δεῖ εἶναί με;
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen pros autous· Ti hoti ezēteite me; ouk ēdeite hoti en tois tou patros mou dei einai me;

paragraphs.text: And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐ συνῆκαν τὸ ῥῆμα ὃ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai autoi ou synēkan to rhēma ho elalēsen autois.

paragraphs.text: And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth; and he was subject unto them: and his mother kept all [these] sayings in her heart.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατέβη μετʼ αὐτῶν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρέθ, καὶ ἦν ὑποτασσόμενος αὐτοῖς. καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ διετήρει πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai katebē metʼ autōn kai ēlthen eis Nazareth, kai ēn hypotassomenos autois. kai hē mētēr autou dietērei panta ta rhēmata tauta en tē kardia autēs.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus advanced in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ Ἰησοῦς προέκοπτεν σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ καὶ χάριτι παρὰ θεῷ καὶ ἀνθρώποις.
paragraphs.translit: Kai Iēsous proekopten sophia kai hēlikia kai chariti para theō kai anthrōpois.
